mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on both teams' possession share and shots volume in the same match sample. The relationship is evaluated as a cross-team asymmetry: Team A's possession-to-shots ratio versus Team B's possession-to-shots ratio, using all-prior and recent-5 windows for both teams.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team holds a dominant possession share, its shots volume rises disproportionately relative to the possession-to-shots ratio of the lower-possession team; the gap between the two ratios widens as the possession differential grows.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A holds a large possession advantage over Team B, but the joint relationship between each team's possession share and their shots volume reveals an asymmetric conversion: Team A's recent possession surge (67.6%) co-occurs with a shots surge (16.6 recent vs 13.1 all-prior), while Team B's possession deficit (37.8% recent) co-occurs with a shots contraction (9.4 recent vs 10.2 all-prior). The mechanism tests whether the joint possession-shots ratio differs systematically across the two sides beyond what each observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single-observable with one band. It requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (possession AND shots) for both sides simultaneously and testing whether their ratio relationship is asymmetric across teams — a two-observable, cross-team joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams' possession share jointly with their shots and shots-on-target counts. Evaluate whether the shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio is higher for the possession-dominant team across historical match samples where a similar possession differential existed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The possession-dominant team's shots-on-target per shot rises relative to the possession-deficient team's ratio; the asymmetry in conversion quality grows with the size of the possession differential.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots-on-target production (5.6 recent, 4.7 all-prior) is elevated relative to its shots volume, while Team B's shots-on-target rate (3.8 recent, 2.9 all-prior) is low relative to its shots volume. The joint relationship between possession dominance and shots-on-target conversion rate differs across the two teams: the dominant-possession team converts a higher share of shots to shots-on-target than the low-possession team.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires three observables jointly (possession, shots, shots_on_target) and a cross-team ratio comparison. Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half (first vs second) jointly for both teams' scoring and conceding rates. Specifically, test the joint pattern: Team A's first-half goals-for rate paired with Team B's first-half goals-against rate, versus Team A's second-half goals-for rate paired with Team B's second-half goals-against rate. This is a two-dimensional half × team-role interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The combined first-half goal environment (Team A scoring + Team B conceding in H1) differs directionally from the combined second-half goal environment, with the second half showing a higher joint conceding exposure for Team B relative to the first half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A scores more goals in the first half (0.684) than the second half (0.750), a relatively balanced split, while Team B scores heavily in the first half (0.382) relative to its second half (0.342), and concedes more in the second half (0.855) than the first (0.566). The joint within-match half-level goal distribution for both teams simultaneously — Team A's first-half scoring rate against Team B's second-half conceding rate, and vice versa — creates a cross-half, cross-team interaction that is not captured by either team's half-level split alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split applied jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously — a two-dimensional conditioning (half × team-side) that cannot be reduced to a single team's half split or a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on half (H1 vs H2) and both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner rates simultaneously. Test whether the combined second-half corner total (Team A FOR + Team B FOR, or equivalently Team A AGAINST + Team B AGAINST) is systematically higher than the first-half combined total when both teams individually show second-half corner concentration.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently show higher second-half corner rates (FOR and AGAINST), the combined second-half corner environment rises above the first-half environment by more than either team's individual half-split would suggest in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Both teams show a second-half corner kick concentration: Team A generates 2.233 corners in H2 vs 1.959 in H1 (FOR), and concedes 2.808 in H2 vs 2.397 in H1 (AGAINST). Team B generates 2.276 in H2 vs 2.039 in H1 (FOR) and concedes 2.987 in H2 vs 2.697 in H1 (AGAINST). The joint half-level corner distribution across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives tests whether the second-half corner environment is amplified when both teams simultaneously exhibit second-half corner concentration tendencies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on half AND both teams' FOR/AGAINST corner rates simultaneously — a two-dimensional (half × dual-team) interaction not reducible to a single team's half split or a single-observable band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on a team's full-match foul rate (as a continuous variable) and test whether the second-half card rate (cards_2h) shows a threshold or non-linear relationship — specifically, whether teams above a foul-rate threshold accumulate cards_2h at an accelerating rate relative to teams below that threshold, rather than a simple linear scaling.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: cards_2h rises with fouls rate but shows a threshold or saturation pattern: below a foul-rate threshold the relationship is weak, but above it cards_2h escalates disproportionately; both teams in this fixture operate above the competition foul baseline, suggesting they sit in the elevated-escalation regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits high fouls (14.2 all-prior, 15.0 recent) and concedes high fouls (13.7 all-prior, 16.6 recent), while Team B commits fewer fouls (12.4 all-prior, 12.6 recent). The joint relationship between a team's foul-committing rate and its second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) tests whether high-foul teams face a non-linear escalation in second-half card exposure — i.e., whether the cards_2h rate saturates or accelerates beyond a foul-rate threshold, rather than scaling linearly. Team A's cards_2h FOR (1.316) and AGAINST (1.421) are both elevated relative to Team B's (1.211 FOR, 1.368 AGAINST), and the competition context cards_2h is 0.75, suggesting both teams operate above the competition norm.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable (fouls × cards_2h) threshold/non-linear relationship, not a single-observable mirror or a simple band split. It requires testing the shape of the fouls-to-cards_2h relationship across the continuous foul-rate distribution, which is structurally richer than any covered single-observable comparison.
